subject: Phased cohort renewal, sprint credits, and auto-renew escape plan
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@acmeretail.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Browne <mike.browne@acmeretail.com>, procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2028-08-01T14:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal & scaling: proposing split term

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the throughput gains and the KV caching profile you showed. We're starting internal planning for our Oct 1 renewal and would like to propose a structure that lets us scale faster while smoothing our budget. High-level ask: can Redwood support a split-term renewal where year 1 is lighter but includes sprint credits to accelerate feature rollouts, and years 2–3 step up commit amounts with an auto-renewing option that we can opt out of with a 60-day notice?

Key constraints from our side:
- Procurement needs predictable fiscal-year invoice cadence (Oct start).
- Security wants isolation on sensitive pipelines (will need dedicated capacity window).
- Ops wants guardrails on burst capacity; we may need short-term bursts during holiday sales.

I've attached our internal forecast (Acme_renewal_v1.xlsx). Can your team draft a sketch (term lengths, ramp schedule, credits, and opt-out mechanics) so we can show finance and security?

Appreciate it —
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Retail
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@acmeretail.com>, Mike Browne <mike.browne@acmeretail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-02T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal & scaling: proposing split term

Laura — thanks, this is super helpful context. I reviewed the forecast and sketched a pragmatic approach that balances predictability with the ability to accelerate. Draft summary below (attached: mmp_acme_v3.docx).

Proposed structure (sketch):
- Term: 3 years total, co-termed to Oct 1 start.
- Year 1 (Pilot ramp): 50% of committed tokens/capacity, includes 120 sprint credits (apply to burst capacity / priority serving) to support holiday rollout.
- Year 2: 100% committed baseline (regular throughput).
- Year 3: 150% committed baseline (growth year) with optional annual true-up.
- Auto-renew: yes, 12-month auto-renew at prevailing pricing unless opted out with 60-day notice prior to renewal window. Opt-out not retroactive; contract remains in effect through the current term.
- Escape / fallback: if capacity constraints occur, Redwood will fall back to verified open-model variants (lower-cost) for non-sensitive traffic and preserve dedicated capacity for tagged sensitive pipelines.

Operational asks for Acme:
- Confirm which pipelines need dedicated isolation (list by name).
- Provide a 90-day rollout plan for year 1 sprint credits usage.
- Decide whether finance prefers annual invoicing or quarterly invoices pro-rated to Oct start.

Next steps and owners:
- Karthik: will propose pricing ladders and prepay/credit mechanics (will attach a term sheet).
- Camila: will outline onboarding and ops checklist for isolated pipelines.
- Naomi (me): will coordinate mutal action plan and draft a compact MMP for sign-off.

If that high-level approach looks viable, we'll produce a short term-sheet and an MMP by EOD Friday.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-08-04T16:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal & scaling: proposing split term — pricing sketch

Laura / Naomi — I put together a concise pricing ladder and mechanics to match Naomi's structure. See attached (pricing_term_sheet_v2.pdf). Highlights below: 

Pricing highlights
- Year 1: 50% committed baseline at 0.85x standard per-token price, plus 120 sprint credits worth ~ $45k of burst capacity (credits apply to priority queue).
- Year 2: Full baseline at standard price; 5% volume discount applied if usage > baseline for two consecutive quarters.
- Year 3: 150% baseline with a 10% commitment discount applied to the incremental portion.
- Prepay vs invoicing: recommend annual prepay for the committed baseline (best unit economics). Quarterly invoicing option available for budget alignment; prepay retains a 3% pricing advantage.
- Auto-renew clause: auto-renews at then-current list price subject to standard CPI cap; opt-out window 60 days. If Acme opts out, year-over-year pricing is reconciled via true-up.

Operational & risk notes
- Dedicated isolation: we can reserve a dedicated pool for up to 12 months with guaranteed latency SLOs; this will require an affirmation of minimum baseline for the dedicated pool.
- Burst capacity during holiday: propose a burst buffer (on-demand) with a 48-hour ramp notice for high-traffic events.

If this looks directionally right, Naomi — can we lock the MMP items and ship a redlineable term sheet to procurement? Laura — happy to jump on a short call to walk through numbers.

Karthik
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-08-09T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal & scaling: proposing split term — ops checklist and onboarding cadence

All — quick ops note to keep things executable on our side. We synced with infra and SRE about the dedicated pool and holiday burst expectations. Actionable items below: 

Onboarding & ops checklist (deliverables)
- Dedicated pipelines: Acme to provide canonical list (names + retention requirements) by Aug 16.
- Capacity ramp schedule: propose quarterly ramp gates (30/60/90 days) during year 1 that trigger autoscaling thresholds.
- SLOs & runbooks: Redwood will produce runbooks for escalation and a 24/7 on-call window for holiday bursts.
- Security: we will provide SOC evidence pack and an HSM/KMS integration checklist (to be completed before dedicated pool activation).

Timeline suggestion
- Aug 9: Agree on MMP and term-sheet redlines.
- Aug 16: Acme provides pipeline list + preferred invoicing cadence.
- Aug 23: Redwood provides final term-sheet (redlineable) and Ops runbook draft.
- Sept 6: Mutual signatures and technical on-boarding begins.

One operational caveat: if Acme chooses quarterly invoicing instead of prepay, we will need a minimum quarterly committed amount for the dedicated pool to keep guaranteed SLOs; Karthik can include language in the sheet.

I'll wait on the pipeline list and will schedule a 30-minute walk-through once we have the MMP.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Customer Success — Onboarding & Adoption
Redwood Inference
